reference.title: Barbell Seated Overhead Triceps Extension
reference.listing: Video (title from the listing URL; the page could not be fetched from this environment, so the movement follows the exercise name and standard coaching)

breathing.pattern: Inhale as the bar lowers behind the head, exhale as you straighten the arms.
breathing.cadence: About 2.3 s down, short pause, about 1.4 s up

prescription.load: Barbell load is user-chosen: pick a weight you can control for every rep with 1-3 reps in reserve (RPE 7-9). Expect to use less than for pushdowns: overhead loads were 34-39% lower in the training study (PubMed 35819335).
prescription.progression: More reps, then 1-2.5 kg more; the training study used 5 sets of 10 at 70% 1RM twice a week

cues.text: Sit tall on the end of a flat bench, feet flat. Hold the bar overhead with straight arms, overhand grip a little narrower than shoulder width.
Breathe in and bend the elbows, lowering the bar behind the head; elbows point up and stay close to the head.
Bar behind the head at about neck height, upper arms beside the ears, trunk tall.
Breathe out and straighten the elbows to press the bar back overhead.
Arms straight but not locked, ribs down; repeat.

mistakes.fix: Keep the elbows pointing up, about head width apart.

mistakes.mistake: Upper arms dropping forward as you press
mistakes.fix: Keep the upper arms beside the head; only the forearms move.
Brace the abs and keep the ribs down; use a lighter bar.
Keep the head neutral; the bar travels behind it.

mistakes.mistake: Bar hitting the back of the head or neck
mistakes.fix: Lower only as far as you can control, with the elbows high.

kinematics.norm: A little narrower than shoulder width (clinical opinion)
Straight but not locked at the top; lower until the bar is behind the head, about 100-120 degrees (clinical opinion)

Arm overhead: the long head is lengthened, which gave more triceps growth than the arm at the side (PubMed 35819335); at 135-180 degrees of shoulder elevation the medial head carried the most force (Kholinne 2018)
The bar passes behind the head without touching it (clinical opinion)
Tall on the end of a flat bench, feet flat (clinical opinion)
Controlled, about 2 s lowering and 1-1.5 s pressing (clinical opinion); the EMG comparison used sets of 7 reps at 70% of 1RM (Boehler 2011)

sources.title: GymVisual, Barbell Seated Overhead Triceps Extension, video (movement reference)

Triceps brachii hypertrophy is substantially greater after elbow extension training performed in the overhead versus neutral arm position (Eur J Sport Sci 2022, DOI 10.1080/17461391.2022.2100279; PubMed 35819335; 21 adults, 12 weeks, cable)

The different role of each head of the triceps brachii muscle in elbow extension (Acta Orthop Traumatol Turc 2018;52(3):201-205; PubMed 29503079; EMG plus OpenSim at 0-180 degrees of shoulder elevation)

Boehler 2011, electromyographic analysis of the triceps brachii muscle during a variety of triceps exercises (MS thesis, University of Wisconsin-La Crosse, ACE-sponsored; 15 women, 8 exercises at 70% 1RM)

cautions: Shoulder pain overhead: switch to a cable or a lying extension (clinical opinion).
Start light: the bar travels behind the head, close to the neck.
Get the bar overhead from a clean press or a partner; never swing it up behind the neck.
Stop if sharp pain, numbness or tingling occurs.
Muscle glow colours and activation curves are illustrative, not measured EMG.
modify: Lower back arching: use a bench with an upright back pad.

muscleNotes.triceps_r: Does the work with the arm overhead, where the long head is lengthened. Twelve weeks of overhead elbow extensions grew the long head about 1.5 times and the whole triceps about 1.4 times more than the same training with the arm at the side (Eur J Sport Sci, PubMed 35819335).
muscleNotes.triceps_l: Does the work with the arm overhead, where the long head is lengthened. Twelve weeks of overhead elbow extensions grew the long head about 1.5 times and the whole triceps about 1.4 times more than the same training with the arm at the side (Eur J Sport Sci, PubMed 35819335).
muscleNotes.ant_deltoid_r: Holds the upper arms up beside the head (clinical opinion).
muscleNotes.ant_deltoid_l: Holds the upper arms up beside the head (clinical opinion).
muscleNotes.lat_deltoid_r: Helps hold the arms overhead (clinical opinion).
muscleNotes.lat_deltoid_l: Helps hold the arms overhead (clinical opinion).
muscleNotes.upper_traps_r: Rotate the shoulder blades upward to keep the arms overhead (clinical opinion).
muscleNotes.upper_traps_l: Rotate the shoulder blades upward to keep the arms overhead (clinical opinion).
muscleNotes.serratus_r: Works with the upper trapezius to hold the shoulder blades in upward rotation (clinical opinion).
muscleNotes.serratus_l: Works with the upper trapezius to hold the shoulder blades in upward rotation (clinical opinion).
muscleNotes.core: Keeps the ribs down so the lower back does not arch.
